title: The fixed-target arrow projection is a right fibration
statement:
Use quasicategories and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplicial map is a right fibration if it has the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $m\geq1$ and $0<j\leq m$. Let $\mathcal D$ be any quasicategory and $T$ a vertex. Define
$$E_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal D}\{T\},$$
where the point $\{T\}\to\mathcal D$ includes all constant simplices at $T$. Then the source evaluation $q_T=\operatorname{ev}_0:E_T\to\mathcal D$ is a right fibration.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13, right-handed assertion; its oriented fiber product is precisely the displayed arrow pullback. Kerodon tag 01KQ (not the unrelated Stacks tag); read online, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ and $0<j\leq m$, and put $i:A=\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow B=\Delta^m$. A lifting square is a map $a:A\to E_T$ and $b:B\to\mathcal D$ with $q_Ta=bi$. The internal-functor definition gives a simplicial map $H:A\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal D$: in degree $n$, for $x\in A_n$ and $s:[n]\to[1]$, evaluate the map $a_n(x):\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ on $(s,\mathrm{id}_{[n]})$. For $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$, naturality gives $a_r(A(\alpha)x)=a_n(x)\circ(\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}\times\Delta(\alpha))$; evaluating this identity at $(s\alpha,\mathrm{id}_{[r]})$ proves the operator identity for $H$. Its endpoint restrictions are $H|_{A\times\{0\}}=bi$ and $H|_{A\times\{1\}}=T$. Using the blunt-join pushout formula of [lem-coef-infinity-blunt-join-comparison], glue $H$, $bi:A\to\mathcal D$, and $T:\Delta^0\to\mathcal D$ to $\widetilde a:A\diamond\Delta^0\to\mathcal D$. Its restriction to $A$ is $bi$, so it glues with $b$ to $\sigma_0:B\amalg_A(A\diamond\Delta^0)\to\mathcal D$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13, unpacking the lifting problem via the blunt join of Notation 4.6.2.3 (01HR); the evaluation and gluing formulas are written explicitly here.

proof.text: The inclusion $i$ is one of the generating horns in the inline definition of right anodyne in [lem-coef-infinity-blunt-join-comparison]. Apply that node to $i$, the quasicategory $\mathcal D$, and $\sigma_0$. Its extension clause, which combines the monomorphic categorical equivalence of Kerodon 01J0 with the extension lemma 01FS, gives $\sigma:B\diamond\Delta^0\to\mathcal D$ with $\sigma\theta_i=\sigma_0$. In particular its restriction to $B$ is $b$, and its restriction to the distinguished terminal point is $T$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13, final sentence: Corollary 4.6.2.14 (01J0) followed by Lemma 4.5.6.2 (01FS).

proof.text:
Let $c_B:B\times\Delta^1\to B\diamond\Delta^0$ be the cylinder map in the blunt-join pushout. Compose the entire cylinder with $\sigma$ to get $H_B=\sigma c_B$; its initial endpoint is $b$ and its terminal endpoint is constant at $T$. For each simplex $x:\Delta^n\to B$, set $\bar a_n(x)=H_B\circ(x\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1})\circ\mathrm{swap}:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$. Precomposing $x$ with any simplicial operator gives the corresponding operator on this map, so the formula defines $\bar a:B\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)$. The terminal restriction is $T$, hence $\bar a$ factors through $E_T$; the initial restriction gives $q_T\bar a=b$. Since $\sigma$ extends $\sigma_0$, $H_B|_{A\times\Delta^1}=H$. For $x\in A_n$, $t:[r]\to[n]$ and $s:[r]\to[1]$, evaluation of its restriction gives
$$\bar a_n(x)_r(s,t)=H_r(A(t)x,s)=a_r(A(t)x)_r(s,\mathrm{id}_{[r]})=a_n(x)_r(s,t),$$
where the last equality is naturality of $a$ for $t$. Thus the maps $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ agree on every simplex, so $\bar a i=a$. This fills the arbitrary horn lifting square and proves the right-fibration assertion.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13, recovering a solution to the original lifting problem; the full cylinder precomposition and factor swap are explicit here.
